services.metaDescription: Year-round pest control in Osceola & Orange Counties for palmetto bugs, ants, spiders & more. Trusted local protection by Orlando Pest Pros for Florida homes.
services.h1: Pest Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: Around Kissimmee, St. Cloud and Orlando there's no real off-season. One afternoon storm floods the mulch beds and American cockroaches aka palmetto bugs are marching for the garage door, ghost ants are back on the coffee maker, and roof rats are running the fence behind the citrus.

We built this plan for stucco homes with lanais, screen enclosures and retention ponds out back. You'll get exterior-first work, a straight explanation of what we saw, and no puffed-up promises. If you've got a US-192 rental with revolving doors, we've seen that mess too.

pests.name: Palmetto Bugs
pests.blurb: Big American cockroaches that breed in sewers, palm boots and damp mulch. On muggy nights they'll fly straight for porch lights and slip under garage doors. We treat harborage along the foundation and mulch edge, dust weep holes and hose bibs, and call out torn screens and bad sweeps.

pests.name: Ghost Ants
pests.blurb: You'll spot them first around the kitchen sink or bath vanity, tiny amber bodies trailing from a wall void or window frame. Spraying the trail just splits them. We track back to moisture, drop sweet bait they carry home, and pull back mulch that's piled against the stucco.

pests.name: Fire Ants
pests.blurb: After a week of storms, mounds blow up along St. Cloud lawns and Kissimmee retention banks. Kids and dogs find them fast. We dust individual mounds and bait foragers around the yard so colonies don't shift ten feet over.

pests.name: Roof Rats
pests.blurb: Roof rats love our attics and orange trees. They'll travel fences and rooflines after dark, so listen for thumps past 10pm and look for black pellets by the water heater. We set traps on their runs, point out chewed soffits and open rooflines, and tell you what brush to cut back.

pests.name: Spiders
pests.blurb: Wolf spiders hunt the garage floor, house spiders string up lanai corners, and we've pulled black widows from meter boxes and stacked pots. We sweep webs, treat eaves and door frames, and tell you to move firewood and dense pots off the wall.

pests.name: Millipedes and Earwigs
pests.blurb: When mulch stays soaked, millipedes curl up by the hundred along thresholds and earwigs tuck into door weatherstripping. I don't broadcast the whole yard. I edge the beds, treat thresholds and expansion joints, and flag sprinklers that never shut off.

pests.name: Silverfish
pests.blurb: They chew book bindings and shirt collars in damp closets and garage boxes. You'll see shed skins and peppery droppings in the tub at night. We dry out the story first, treat baseboards and wall voids lightly, and keep the exterior tight so more don't wander in.

sections.heading: No winter kill-off around Orlando
body: Up north a hard freeze resets things. Here ghost ants and Argentine ants feed straight through January in wall voids and under pavers. You'll think it's quiet in December, but they're tucked deeper until heat and rain pull them back out.

Add stucco that holds humidity, tile roofs with gaps at the ridge, mulch volcanoes around palms, and a retention pond or conservation strip behind the fence. That's a palmetto bug and roof rat setup. One spray won't hold. Steady exterior work after each storm cycle will.

sections.heading: Our visit routine from curb to kitchen
body: I walk the whole exterior first. Door sweeps, garage seal, weep holes, hose bibs, electric penetrations, lanai screen base and the mulch line. I'm looking for busy ant trails, webbed eaves, droppings, and water sitting in bromeliads or saucers.

Treatment stays outside as much as possible, foundation band, entry points and harborage, then light spot work inside kitchens, baths and the garage only where you've seen activity. I sweep webs down, jot fixes you can do with caulk and mesh, and keep notes so next visit isn't starting blind.

sections.heading: Careful around kids, pets and backyard wildlife
body: Most Orlando yards have a dog, a lizard crew and pollinators working the porterweed. I don't blanket the lawn. Crack and crevice work, targeted granules in beds away from play spots, and I skip butterfly plantings, veggie boxes and the pool deck edge when you ask me to.

You'll get a plain rundown of what went where and when to water or let the dog back on the treated band. If you've got a pond, tortoise burrow or a lanai cat that licks everything, point it out and I'll route around it.

process.detail: We check attic hatch, garage, kitchen and baths inside, then foundation, mulch, fence and screen enclosure outside. You tell us what's bugging you and we show you what we're finding.
No package mumbo jumbo. We'll say what's active, what's only conducive, what we'll treat today and what you can trim, seal or dry out yourself.

We lay the protective band, treat entry points and harborage, sweep webs and handle interior hot spots with bait or light spot care. If the screen door hangs open all day, we'll tell you, that's how palmettos stroll in.
Florida pressure rebuilds after every storm. We come back on schedule, tweak for swarm season or heavy rain, and if something flares between visits you've got us to call for a recheck.

faqs.q: Why do I need pest control all year in Central Florida?
faqs.a: There's no freeze to knock colonies back. Ghost ants, palmettos and roof rats just shift from mulch and ponds into walls and attics.

faqs.q: Is your treatment safe around kids and pets?
faqs.a: Yes. We spot-treat cracks, weep holes and entry points, skip play areas and gardens, and we'll tell you when pets can go back out.

faqs.q: Why do palmetto bugs fly inside during summer?
faqs.a: American cockroaches live in sewers, palms and mulch and fly on humid nights. They'll push under garage doors and torn lanai screens.

faqs.q: Do I need to leave my home during service?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most work is outside along the foundation and lanai. We'll flag if a kitchen or bath spot needs a few minutes to dry.

faqs.q: What if pests come back between visits?
faqs.a: Storms stir everything up. Call us, tell us where you're seeing activity, and we'll come back to recheck the spots we cover.

spotlight.heading: Your treatment calendar around Orlando
body: Florida bugs don't take quarters off, so we shift focus as rain and heat shift. Spring brings ant trails and termite swarms, summer brings palmetto pressure, fall brings rats and spiders inside.
points: Jan to Mar: dust weep holes, bait ghost and Argentine ants, check attic for roof rats nesting early.
Apr to Jun: renew foundation band before rains, treat mulch edge for palmettos, flag tubes from Eastern subterranean or Formosan termites.
Jul to Sep: knock back fire ant mounds, sweep lanai webs, re-treat thresholds after storms wash through.
Oct to Dec: trap and seal for roof rats moving in, clear garage harborage, tighten door sweeps.

services.name: Termite Control
services.title: Termite Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL | Orlando Pest Pros
services.metaDescription: Protect your Central Florida home from subterranean & Formosan termites with expert inspections, bait systems & barriers by Orlando Pest Pros near Orlando.
services.h1: Termite Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: You won't hear Eastern subterranean termites chewing. You'll see what they leave behind after an afternoon storm pushes a swarm, wings on the lanai sill, a pencil-wide mud tube up the stucco behind the mulch bed. That's the norm from Kissimmee to Winter Park, and Formosans make it worse.

We've crawled enough garages off US-192 and block homes with lanai additions to know where they hide. We'll tap baseboards, probe door frames, walk the soil line and irrigation heads with you, then tell you straight what we found and what will hold in sandy soil.

pests.name: Subterranean Termites
pests.blurb: Eastern subterranean termites nest in sandy soil and run mud tubes up block and stucco to hit framing. They don't need much, just soil contact and damp mulch. We break a tube to check for live workers, tap baseboards, and mark leaky hose bibs and grade issues.

pests.name: Formosan Termites
pests.blurb: Formosans build huge colonies and they'll nest right in a wall void or soffit if AC condensation keeps it damp. We check rooflines, flat roof tie-ins, and laundry wall voids with a moisture meter, because that's where we've found carton nests that never touched soil.

pests.name: Drywood Termites
pests.blurb: West Indian drywood termites don't use soil at all. They live inside fascia, trim, cabinets, and attic trusses. You'll spot them by tiny ridged pellets under kick-out holes. We probe the wood, vacuum old frass to confirm it's active, and inject the gallery.

pests.name: Dampwood Termites
pests.blurb: Dampwoods show up where wood's stayed wet, rotted eave ends, fence boards touching stucco, or a shower that's leaked for months. Colonies stay small but they mean you've got rot to fix. We'll call out the repair and treat what's active.

pests.name: Carpenter Ants (Often Confused With Termites)
pests.blurb: Every May we get calls about termite swarmers that turn out to be Florida carpenter ants. Ants have pinched waists and elbowed antennae, termites don't. We check for sawdust piles and smooth galleries in damp window sills and lanai framing, then bait the trail instead of selling you a termite job you don't need.

sections.heading: Spring swarm season around Orlando
body: After a warm rain you'll find them stuck in window tracks, lanai screens, and cobwebs by the porch light. Eastern subterraneans usually fly in daytime spring showers, Formosans fly on humid May to June nights. Either way, a pile of clear wings on a sill means a mature colony is close.

Don't vacuum it all up before we look. Scoop a few wings and a couple dead swarmers into a baggie, note the room and time, and check the garage stem wall and front mulch line for fresh tubes. Indoor swarmers nearly always mean they're already inside the walls.

sections.heading: Bait stations versus liquid soil treatments in sandy soil
body: Baits fit a lot of Kissimmee and St. Cloud lots because our sand won't hold a trench and the water table sits high near ponds and ditches. We space stations 10 to 15 feet around the slab, pop them every visit, and let foragers carry the bait back. You'll see us probing mulch beds and edging, not tearing up the lanai pavers.

Liquids still shine on clean, well-graded slabs with good soil access. We trench and rod along the footing, treat bath traps and plumbing penetrations, and tie it into stucco weep screed height. On the walkthrough we'll show you irrigation heads, grade, and pond setback, then pick what will survive afternoon downpours at your place.

sections.heading: WDO reports that keep closings on track
body: Around Osceola and Orange, most resale deals want a WDO, especially block ranches with wood additions and US-192 rentals turned flips. We inspect accessible attic, garage, lanai tie-ins, and soil line, tapping trim and lifting insulation edges where we can. You'll get photos of live tubes, old damage, frass, and wood-to-soil contact.

Our report spells it in plain English for buyer, seller, and agent. If we find Formosan carton material or active subterraneans, we list the fix, the treatment choice, and what the seller's handyman should repair first. No scare talk, just what the lender needs to clear.

process.detail: We walk the mulch line, stucco weep, lanai footers, and garage stem walls, then head inside to tap baseboards and probe door casings and bath traps. You'll see the moisture readings around AC lines right with us.
You'll get phone photos of tubes, wings, pellets, or chew, plus what we didn't find. We lay out bait, liquid, or spot wood treatment for your block and roof type, with cost and upkeep side by side.

We set stations flush with turf so you won't clip them with the mower, or we trench tight to the footing and seal drill holes in lanai slabs. We flag irrigation and pet bowls first, then rake the mulch back.

Florida pressure doesn't quit, so we return to check stations, re-sight the soil line, and look for fresh wings after spring swarms. If you add a garden bed or regrade for drainage, we adjust the plan on the spot.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have termites or flying ants?
faqs.a: Termites have straight waists, straight antennae, and equal-size wings that fall off in piles. Ants have pinched waists and elbowed antennae. Save a few in a baggie for us to ID under magnification.

faqs.q: What are mud tubes on my block wall or foundation?
faqs.a: They're soil tunnels subterraneans build over block and stucco to reach wood. Break a small piece, active tubes get rebuilt in days. Leave some intact so we can confirm.

faqs.q: Are Formosan termites worse than regular subterranean termites?
faqs.a: Yes, Formosan colonies run bigger and can chew faster, sometimes nesting in roofs without soil contact. Steady bait or a sound liquid zone plus moisture fixes still control them.

faqs.q: Will mulch and irrigation around my home attract termites?
faqs.a: Thick mulch on stucco and daily sprays that keep footers soggy sure help them. Pull mulch back 6 inches, keep soil below siding, and aim heads out. We'll tune it on the visit.

faqs.q: Do I need a WDO inspection when buying in Kissimmee or Orlando?
faqs.a: Most deals here include one, and many lenders want it with our pressure. We document live signs and old damage with photos and list next steps for closing.

spotlight.heading: Four termite signs Orlando homeowners spot first
body: Grab a flashlight after an afternoon storm and walk the garage stem wall, lanai footers, and front mulch line. Most Kissimmee infestations show themselves right there if you know what you're seeing.
points: Pencil-wide mud tubes climbing block, stucco, or garage walls
Clear wings piled on sills, in cobwebs, or around porch lights
Tiny dry piles of ridged pellets under fascia or window trim
Baseboards that sound hollow or blister when you tap them

services.name: Mosquito Control
services.title: Mosquito Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL | Orlando Pest Pros
services.metaDescription: Enjoy your backyard again with mosquito control in Osceola & Orange Counties for ponds, lawns & patios by Orlando Pest Pros. Control, not empty promises in FL.
services.h1: Mosquito Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: In Kissimmee and St. Cloud, mosquitoes don't travel far. They hatch in your bromeliads, saucers, and clogged gutters, then rest in shady St. Augustine until you step onto the lanai.

We'll tell you straight. No spray keeps every mosquito out when you're backed to a retention pond or ditch. Our barrier work plus water hunting cuts the biting way down so evenings outside feel normal again.

pests.name: Mosquitoes
pests.blurb: Asian tiger mosquitoes do most of the daytime biting around Orlando patios. They breed in a saucer of water and they'll sit under hibiscus, arecas, and screen frames till dusk. We coat those leaf undersides and flip the saucers they came from.

pests.name: Biting Midges
pests.blurb: Biting midges breed in damp mulch and muck along retention ponds and lake edges. They slip right through normal pool screens. We treat the shady damp line and still corners, and we're blunt when a fan will help more than spray.

pests.name: No-See-Ums
pests.blurb: No-see-ums hit hardest at dawn and dusk and leave ankle welts way bigger than the bug. They stack up where air goes still behind fences and enclosures. We treat low shrubs and patio edges and point out where to open airflow.

pests.name: Stable Flies and Other Yard Biters
pests.blurb: If you've got dogs, backyard chickens, or fresh grass piles, stable flies will find you. They chew ankles near kennels and compost and breed in wet clippings. We treat fence shade and kennel edges and flag the cleanup that stops the next batch.

pests.name: Ticks in Shady Yards
pests.blurb: Lone star ticks wait on palmetto fronds, mulch beds, and fence lines where dogs and raccoons run. Tall grass and leaf litter make it worse. On mosquito stops we check those edges, note what to rake back, and treat harborage to cut hitchhikers.

sections.heading: Most biters hatched within a block of your patio
body: In Celebration, Buenaventura Lakes, and south Orlando we pull larvae from bromeliad cups, pot saucers, kid toys, grill covers, tarps, and the low lip of stucco where irrigation pools. Roadside ditches and retention ponds behind US-192 rentals stay wet all summer.

We walk the full lot with you, tip what holds water, and mark what needs a gutter scoop or a trim. Adults drift over from neighbor yards on calm nights, so we note that too instead of pretending your fence stops them.

sections.heading: Barrier spray lowers numbers, it doesn't dome the yard
body: We mist the undersides of shrubs, arecas, jasmine, and fence-line foliage where mosquitoes sit out the heat, plus the shady sides of screen enclosures and lanai posts. Landing there is what does them in, so coverage stays where you actually sit.

Afternoon storms wash residue off and hatch a new batch within days. Ponds and conservation swales keep sending adults in. You'll feel far fewer bites, but you'll still see some after heavy rain and that's normal.

sections.heading: Summer rain sets the schedule
body: June through September we stay tight, usually every three to four weeks, because each downpour refills cups fast in this heat. We recheck bromeliads, gutters, and toys that filled since last time.
In drier months we can stretch it and lean on trimming and drainage. Your timing depends on pond exposure, shade, and how often the kids and dogs are out back, not some one-size route sheet.

process.detail: We start at the gate, check toys, tarps, saucers, gutters, and bromeliads, then push into shady shrubs, mulch beds, and the lanai edge. You'll hear exactly where we think your pressure's coming from.
We dump what we can, brush saucers, clear tarp pockets, and flag dense arecas or jasmine that need lifting. Small drainage fixes near stucco and downspouts get written down so you don't forget.

process.step: Lay the barrier where they rest
process.detail: We treat leaf undersides, ground cover, fence lines, and patio perimeters, easing off blooms, veggie beds, and the pool coping. Pets stay inside till dry, and we close gates behind us.
We come back through season to refresh the barrier and hunt new water. Between stops, dump toys after rain, refresh bowls, and tell us if bites spike. We'll say if you need us sooner.

faqs.q: Can you get rid of all mosquitoes in my yard?
faqs.a: No. Ponds, ditches, and neighbor yards around Osceola and Orange keep sending them in. We cut biting pressure way down so patios stay usable, but a few drifters after rain are normal.

faqs.q: How long does a barrier treatment last?
faqs.a: Usually a few weeks. Afternoon storms, irrigation, and fast growth wear it down. We time summer returns every three to four weeks and recheck water each stop.

faqs.q: Is mosquito treatment safe for my garden and pond?
faqs.a: We keep spray off blooms, veggies, and open water and stick to resting leaves and shade. Show us ponds, butterfly plants, and bowls on the walk and we'll work around them.

faqs.q: Why are mosquitoes worse after summer storms?
faqs.a: Rain refills saucers, gutters, and ditches, and warm water hatches eggs in days. Adults scatter to shrubs, then slide back to patios on calm nights.

faqs.q: What can I do between visits to help?
faqs.a: Dump toys and tarps, refresh bowls and birdbaths, clean gutters, and lift low shrubs. If bites jump after a storm, call us and we'll judge timing for the next stop.

spotlight.heading: What our tech does from driveway to back fence
body: Your tech grabs the hose and walks shade first. Side yards with arecas, back fence with jasmine, lanai posts, under the trampoline, then the retention edge if you've got one. He's flipping saucers and checking bromeliad cups as he goes.

He sprays leaf undersides and fence shade where mosquitoes loaf, eases off the pool deck, veggie beds, and butterfly lantana, and asks you to keep dogs in till dry. Gate latched, note left on what refilled.
points: Treats: leaf undersides, arecas, jasmine, fence shade, lanai posts
Skips or shields: pool water, coping, pet bowls, veggie and pollinator beds
Always checks: bromeliads, saucers, gutters, tarps, ditch edge
Leaves you with: what held water and when to call after storms

services.name: Rodent Control
services.title: Rodent Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL | Orlando Pest Pros
services.metaDescription: Trusted rodent control in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL from Orlando Pest Pros. We remove roof rats and mice, seal entry points, and restore attics safely.
services.h1: Rodent Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: Roof rats don't take a season off in Osceola and Orange Counties. Backyard citrus, palm fronds on tile, mulch beds and retention ponds give them food and cover right against your walls.
We've pulled nests out of stucco-home attics from St. Cloud to Winter Garden. We find the chew marks and pellets, trap what's inside, then seal the gaps so the next family can't move in.

pests.name: Roof Rats
pests.blurb: You'll hear them after 10 p.m. racing above the bedroom. They leave blunt pellets under citrus trees and gnaw marks on soffit vents. We run traps in the attic, not poison in insulation, and point out which limbs gave them roof access.

pests.name: Norway Rats
pests.blurb: Bigger and low to the ground. Look for burrow holes by slabs and sheds and greasy rub along garage edges. We've trapped them along canal lots and pond banks where pet bowls sit out all night.

pests.name: House Mice
pests.blurb: They slip through a pencil-width gap under a door or around a sink pipe. You'll find rice-sized droppings in drawers and chewed corners on cereal boxes. We seal those pipe chases and set traps behind stoves where they actually travel.

pests.name: Cotton Rats
pests.blurb: They live in overgrown lots and pond banks on the rural edge past St. Cloud. An afternoon storm floods their cover and they'll bolt for sheds and lanais. Clear the weeds and tighten shed bases and most stay outside where they belong.

sections.heading: Where Central Florida rats slip inside
body: On block and stucco homes I check the same spots first. Lifted tile edges, chewed soffit vents and the gap where AC lines punch through stucco. Roof rats run citrus limbs and fence tops straight to openings you'll miss from the ground.

Down low it's garage doors that don't seal, torn lanai screens and open pipe chases. Add fallen oranges and a dog bowl left out overnight and you've set a table. Once one rat runs it, that scent trail pulls others for months.

sections.heading: Trapping catches rats. Sealing keeps them out.
body: I won't sell you traps alone. Without sealing, a Kissimmee attic or US-192 rental just refills because breeding never pauses here.

We close eaves, pipe entries and garage corners with steel mesh and flashing that'll hold up in humidity and afternoon storms. We add vent covers and door sweeps, then show you which palm fronds and vines to cut back from the roof.

sections.heading: What rat mess does to an attic
body: Rat urine soaks into blown insulation and the smell hangs in our humidity. You'll see matted trails, pellets in soffit corners and chewed wire sheathing. That odor tells the next roof rats this attic is safe.

After the attic goes quiet we pull droppings and nest fluff with HEPA vacs and gloves, treat stained spots and flag thin spots in insulation. You'll get photos and plain advice on storage and vents so it stays dry.

process.detail: We walk the roofline, lift tile edges, scope the attic for rub marks and pellets, and check garage seals and AC penetrations. You'll see photos of every gap we find.
We set snap traps and enclosed stations in the attic and along runs, out of reach of kids and pets. We don't toss poison in insulation. We come back and shift traps till the scratching stops.
We close gaps with steel mesh, flashing and sealant rated for Florida heat and rain. We'll fix soffit vents, pipe collars and garage edges, then tell you what brush to cut back from the roof.
We bag droppings, pull nesting fluff and wipe stained wood. You'll get simple habits that work here, like picking citrus fast and locking trash before nightfall.

faqs.q: Why do I hear scratching in my attic at night?
faqs.a: That's classic roof rats. They nest in insulation and forage after dark, and citrus keeps them active all year.

faqs.q: Are rodents a year round problem near Orlando?
faqs.a: Yes. Mild winters don't stop breeding here. Fallen citrus, pet food and trash feed them every month.

faqs.q: Will traps alone solve a rat problem?
faqs.a: No. Traps thin numbers but don't close gaps, so new rats follow old scent trails back in.

faqs.q: Is attic cleanup really needed after rats leave?
faqs.a: Most times, yes. Soiled insulation holds odor that pulls rats back, so we'll clear debris and sanitize.

faqs.q: How can I keep mice out of my kitchen?
faqs.a: Don't leave dry goods open. Seal containers, caulk sink pipe gaps and cut pantry clutter.

spotlight.heading: Rats use the same four doors
body: Most Osceola and Orange block homes aren't wide open. They've got small construction gaps up top and around utilities, and roof rats need less than an inch.
We don't fog the attic and hope. We fit metal and sealant that survives gnawing and summer storms.
points: Roofline gaps: steel mesh and flashing tucked under lifted tile, not foam
AC line penetrations: sealed collars where lines punch through stucco
Garage door seals: new sweeps and side seals that close night gaps
Soffit vents: tight metal covers that still breathe but block gnawing

services.name: Bed Bug Treatment
services.title: Bed Bug Treatment in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL | Orlando Pest Pros
services.metaDescription: Trusted bed bug treatment in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL. Thorough inspections with heat and conventional solutions for homes and Orlando rentals done right.
services.h1: Bed Bug Treatment in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: Found rust-colored smears on the sheets after a week on US-192 or a cruise out of Port Canaveral? That's how most bed bug jobs start for us in Kissimmee and St. Cloud. Folks feel embarrassed, but there's no reason to be. These bugs ride in luggage, laundry bags, and used furniture, and a clean house won't stop them.

We're Orlando Pest Pros, and we work houses, apartments, and short-term rentals all through Osceola and Orange Counties. You'll get a straight answer on what's a bed bug and what's a carpet beetle, plus a plan that fits the room and your turnover schedule. No panic, no judgment, just a careful check and clear next steps.

pests.name: Bed Bugs
pests.blurb: Bed bugs are flat, reddish-brown, apple-seed sized hiders that feed at night. We pull them from mattress seams, box spring tack strips, headboard screw holes, and couch piping. Don't expect winter to slow them down here. One mated female in a suitcase from a Lake Buena Vista turnover can seed a whole bedroom in weeks.

pests.name: Signs of Infestation
pests.blurb: Most bedrooms we check in Kissimmee show the same early tells. Clustered welts after sleep, black fecal dots and rusty smears on sheets, papery skins stuck in seam folds, a sweet musty odor near a heavy harborage. Look behind the headboard, inside nightstand joints, and where baseboard meets stucco. Daylight checks miss most of it.

pests.name: Common Look-Alikes
pests.blurb: We get plenty of false alarms. Carpet beetle larvae, spider beetles, booklice from damp baths, and baby German cockroaches all get blamed on bed bugs. Beetle fuzz leaves skins and chews fibers but doesn't bite. Young roaches run fast and hang in kitchens. Slip what you found in a zip bag without squashing it and we'll ID it under light.

sections.heading: How bed bugs ride through the Orlando tourism corridor
body: Tourist turnover is fuel. A guest picks up a few bugs in a hotel, vacation home, or cruise transfer, then drops them in a Kissimmee rental off US-192, a condo in Celebration, or a place near Lake Buena Vista. Cleaners flip the unit, next family checks in, and the bugs have fresh blood and new luggage to ride.

Once they're in town, they move with people and stuff. Visiting relatives, college kids home for break, roommates shifting apartments, all of it helps them hop room to room. Used headboards, mattresses, and couches from Marketplace are another big source. That's why we check beyond the main bed. We trace laundry routes, guest beds, and couches.

sections.heading: Heat work compared with conventional bed bug work
body: Whole-room heat brings beds, furniture, and wall voids up to lethal temps and holds them there while we monitor probes in seams and clutter. It kills eggs and active bed bugs together, even where dusts and liquids can't reach. For cluttered rooms or US-192 rentals that need fast turnover with little residue, it's often the cleanest reset.

Conventional work uses targeted liquids, void dusts, and growth regulators with tight prep and a follow-up visit. It costs less, leaves residual control, and suits early catches or rooms full of heat-sensitive gear. A lot of homes land on a blend. We'll tell you straight which fits your layout, bug pressure, and guest calendar, because prep and follow-through decide it either way.

sections.heading: Prep that actually helps, and why store sprays backfire
body: Wash bedding and clothes on hot, dry on high heat, then bag clean loads sealed. Pull beds a few inches off walls, cut clutter around sleeping spots, and make mattress platforms and storage reachable. For rentals, get cleaners, handymen, and managers on the same day so every sleeping area gets opened and checked at once.

Store sprays and foggers push bed bugs deeper into baseboards and next rooms. Foggers coat the air and miss harborages. Light repeat spraying builds resistance and leaves eggs alive. Encasements help for monitoring, but they won't end it alone. Pro equipment, product rotation, and a patient recheck are what break the cycle.

process.detail: We flashlight mattress seams, tack strips, headboard voids, nightstand joints, couch seams, baseboards, and luggage spots. You see what we see, bed bugs or look-alike, before we talk price.
We map hit rooms and lay out heat, conventional, or a blend for your layout and rental calendar. You get a short prep sheet, pet and kid notes, and clear guest messaging for hosts.

We treat bed frames, seams, cracks, outlets nearby, and adjoining living areas with tight coverage. On heat jobs we watch probes room by room. On conventional jobs we place dusts and residuals right where bed bugs travel.
We come back, check interceptors and old harborages, and handle lingering spots. You get simple habits for travel, used furniture, and turnover laundry that cut reintroduction risk.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have bed bugs or something else?
faqs.a: Check for clustered welts, rusty smears and black fecal spots on sheets, shed skins in mattress seams, and live bugs behind headboards. Carpet beetles and baby German roaches fool folks often, so get an ID before you spray or toss furniture.

faqs.q: Do I have to throw away my mattress and couch?
faqs.a: Usually you can keep it. If the mattress is solid and seams are intact, we'll treat it. We'll only flag replacement when framing is cracked, heavily harbored, or taped together past saving.

faqs.q: Is heat treatment better than sprays?
faqs.a: Heat kills all stages in one visit, even eggs in seams, but you can't use it around some electronics and heat-sensitive items. Conventional work costs less and leaves residual control, though it needs prep and a follow-up. We'll match it to the room.

faqs.q: Can you treat vacation rentals and apartments discreetly?
faqs.a: Yes. We service US-192 rentals, condos, and apartments from Kissimmee to Orlando. We time visits around cleanings, keep gear discreet, and loop in your host or manager so turnover stays on track.

faqs.q: What should I do after treatment to prevent them from coming back?
faqs.a: Travel with luggage on racks, dry trip clothes on high heat, and inspect used headboards and couches before they come inside. Keep clutter off bedroom floors and call fast if spots show up again.

spotlight.heading: How to check a hotel room in 5 minutes
body: Leave your bag in the tub or on tile while you look. Tile gives bed bugs nowhere to hide during those first minutes in a Kissimmee motel off US-192 or a resort in Celebration.
If you find live bugs or fresh black spots, ask for a room far from that one and tell the desk plainly. Don't buy a store spray for insurance, it scatters them deeper and won't touch eggs.
points: Pull back sheets and run a card along mattress seams and tags for live bugs and black spots
Shine your phone light behind headboard edges, nightstand joints, and alarm clock seams
Keep luggage on the metal rack pulled from the wall, never on the bed or carpet
At home, dry all trip clothes on high heat and check bag seams outside the bedroom

services.title: Wildlife Removal in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL | Orlando Pest Pros
services.metaDescription: Humane wildlife removal in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL for raccoons, opossums, armadillos, squirrels. Safe trapping, exclusion & attic cleanup by local pros
services.h1: Humane Wildlife Removal in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: If you're hearing heavy thumps over the lanai at 2 a.m. or waking up to mulch beds plowed like someone ran a tiller through them, that's a normal Tuesday around Kissimmee and St. Cloud. Raccoons, opossums, gray squirrels, and armadillos don't take a season off here. They den in block-home attics, under sheds, and along retention ponds where grubs and trash never run out.

We've pulled raccoons out of soffits chewed open after an afternoon storm and screened armadillo digs under sheds at US-192 rentals. Our fix is simple and humane. Live traps or one-way doors where they fit, then we seal the hole with real material so you don't pay for the same job twice. If it thumps, scratches, or stinks, we'll put eyes on it and tell you straight what's living there.

pests.name: Armadillos
pests.blurb: You'll know armadillos by cone-shaped holes in the turf and mulch kicked across the driveway overnight. They hunt grubs and earthworms after rain and wedge under shed slabs and decks. We live-trap the digger, backfill burrows, and set a buried L-footer of hardware cloth so it can't bulldoze back in.

pests.name: Opossums
pests.blurb: Opossums love the gap under a shed or lanai enclosure where it's dark and close to cat food. They don't chew much, but they leave greasy rubs, droppings, and that sour trash odor, plus tipped cans. We cage-trap gently, release on site per state rules, and screen the skirting so the next one can't move in.

pests.name: Raccoons
pests.blurb: A mama raccoon will peel back a loose soffit or lift a storm-softened shingle to den right over your bedroom. Then comes night thumping, torn trash, missing citrus, and a latrine in the attic insulation. We set shaded live traps, pull the family intact, and close the entry with metal and sealant that claws can't shred.

pests.name: Gray Squirrels
pests.blurb: Gray squirrels hit in daylight. They run oaks and power lines onto the roof, chew through fascia and stucco returns, and shred insulation into nests. You'll hear rolling and gnawing by morning and find tooth marks on the eave. We trap out, then patch chewed wood with metal-backed repairs and tell you which limb to cut back.

pests.name: Flying Squirrels
pests.blurb: Flying squirrels are tiny, nocturnal, and never alone. A colony sounds like soft pattering and squeaks near 11 p.m., with pellet droppings and musky odor in the insulation. We don't cage-trap whole colonies. We fit one-way doors over their seam gaps, let them file out, then seal every quarter-inch seam.

pests.name: Bats
pests.blurb: Bats squeeze through a 3/8-inch gap at the gable or ridge and streak stucco with guano. Florida protects them, so there's no trapping like raccoons. During the allowed season we mount one-way exits, let the colony leave to feed, then seal the roofline and clean accessible guano. Timing matters, and we'll tell you if you've got to wait a few weeks.

sections.heading: The usual suspects around Kissimmee attics and yards
body: There's no off-season here. Live near a retention pond, canal, or oak hammock in Buenaventura Lakes or Hunters Creek and you've got roof rats in the citrus, raccoons in the trash, and armadillos working the mulch beds after every afternoon storm. Screen enclosures and lanais help folks, not wildlife. One lifted vent or sun-baked soffit seam is all it takes.

Signs tell us who's in there before we ever set a trap. Armadillos leave pitted lawns and soil fanned under the shed. Raccoons thump hard after dark and leave big latrines. Opossums shuffle and stink. Gray squirrels chew in daylight and leave 2-inch holes with tooth marks. Flying squirrels and bats whisper at night and leave pellet droppings or guano streaks on stucco. We'll show you the rubs and droppings so you know we're not guessing.

sections.heading: Humane work that follows Florida FWC guidance
body: We ID first, then pick the least stressful way out. That's usually a shaded live cage trap checked daily or a one-way door over the entry so the animal leaves and can't get back in. We don't use poison. It causes a slow death and it kills owls, hawks, and your neighbor's cat when a poisoned animal gets eaten. Traps, droppings, and nesting material get handled with gloves, respirators, and bags, not bare hands.

Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission guidance calls the next step. Raccoons, bats, and a few other species can't legally be hauled to the woods and let go, since that spreads disease and dumps a problem on someone else. In practice that means release on the same property where allowed or humane handling by a pro, plus timed exclusion for bats. You'll get a straight answer from us on what's allowed for your animal, and we put sealing first so you're not trapping forever.

sections.heading: Sealing the house so they stay out
body: Trapping alone buys you a month. The next raccoon will test the same soft soffit. We've learned to close everything while we're there. Soffit seams, fascia gaps, roof returns, AC line penetrations, and gable vents get metal, hardware cloth, and sealant that teeth can't chew. Sheds and decks get screened with buried wire. For armadillos we trench a low L-footer and rake out harborage. Cut limbs 8 feet off the roof, lock trash lids, and bring pet bowls in at night.

Then we deal with the mess they left. Raccoon latrines and opossum droppings soak insulation and stink up drywall, and that odor pulls in palmetto bugs and roof rats fast in this heat, while soggy fascia invites Formosan termites. We pull accessible soiled insulation, bag nesting debris, treat with enzyme deodorizer, and flag chewed wire sleeves and stained decking with photos. You won't wonder what still needs a handyman. It'll be sealed, drier, and quiet.

process.detail: We ladder the eaves, pop the attic hatch, and walk the fence, shed, and lanai base. You're getting photos of tracks, droppings, rubs, and chew holes, plus a call on species and if babies are inside. That decides trap versus door, and we won't seal young in.

We set cabled live traps in shade or bolt a one-way door right on the hole. Traps get checked daily, animals stay calm and covered, and moms with kits get extra care so nobody's left squealing in a wall. No poisons, ever.

Once it's quiet, we close it for real. Galvanized flashing, quarter-inch hardware cloth, vent guards, and polyurethane sealant on stucco gaps, not foam alone. Armadillo runs get a buried footer. We'll mark limbs and trash habits bringing them in.

process.step: Clean up and keep them off
process.detail: We bag accessible droppings and nest fluff, spray enzyme treatment for odor, and vacuum guano dust where we can reach. You'll leave with a short list. Lock cans, pick citrus, feed pets inside, keep mulch pulled off the slab.

faqs.q: Is wildlife removal humane and what happens to the animals?
faqs.a: Yes. We use live cage traps and one-way doors, no poisons, and handle animals quietly for on-site release where allowed. Then we seal entries so you don't get repeats.

faqs.q: Why can I not just catch a raccoon and release it in the woods?
faqs.a: State rules don't allow moving raccoons off your property, since it spreads disease and they often die or trek back. We'll explain your lawful options and focus on removal plus sealing.

faqs.q: How can I tell what is living in my attic?
faqs.a: Listen for timing. Gray squirrels move by day, raccoons and flying squirrels thump and patter at night. Chewed soffits, droppings, and musky odor confirm it, but let us inspect the attic safely.

faqs.q: How do you stop armadillos from tearing up my lawn again?
faqs.a: We trap the active digger, backfill burrows, and add a buried footer around sheds and beds. Pick fallen fruit and thin dense cover. Grub killer alone won't stop them.

faqs.q: Do you clean up droppings, odor, and attic mess after removal?
faqs.a: Yes. We remove accessible droppings and nesting debris, treat odor, and flag stained insulation and chewed materials. Sealing at the same time keeps squirrels and rats from moving back in.

spotlight.heading: We get them out, then we keep them out
body: Raccoons and a few other species can't legally be relocated in Florida, so hauling them to the woods isn't an option. Our work centers on humane removal on site and sealing the house so the next family can't move in.
That means covered live traps or one-way doors, daily checks, and metal-backed patches the same visit the attic goes quiet.
points: Shaded live traps, checked daily, no poisons
One-way doors for squirrels and bats in season
Metal, hardware cloth, and sealant on soffits and vents
Photos of entries and a simple prevention list
